One of the year’s most important interventions was a 
risk pre-filter designed to prioritise portfolio quality over 
near-term disbursal volume.
The framework operates before an application reaches 
the lending partner. It evaluates applicants using models 
developed from Paisabazaar’s historical outcome data 
and deprioritises profiles exhibiting a higher probability 
of early delinquency.
The framework currently filters ~ 8% of applicants 
who may otherwise meet partner approval criteria, 
with an estimated impact of around 10% on disbursal 
volumes. This cohort has exhibited close to three times 
the six-month delinquency of the broader approved 
population.
We chose to do it because that cohort shows close to 
three times the six-month delinquency of the baseline 
approved population. Approving them would have 
produced a good quarter and a bad year.
This approach supports more measured growth, 
balancing near-term volumes with the quality and 
sustainability of the portfolio.
The PB Risk Score Filter intercepts applicants ahead of lender 
decisioning, deprioritises high-risk profiles, re-routes better users and 
tags micro-segments. Independently validated by Ernst & Young for 
discriminative power.

Credit awareness is most effective when consumers

information. In 2025, we launched the Credit Premier

timed to the cricket season.
By bringing the familiarity and excitement of cricket

their Credit Score in a way that felt less like a financial 
exercise and more like a nation-wide contest.

PB Connect: Enabling Scalable, Retail-Led Growth
PB Connect initially built scale through a concentrated 
set of wholesale partnerships. This provided an efficient 
starting point and helped the business develop market 
knowledge, customer understanding and fulfilment 
capabilities. 
During FY26, PB Connect began transitioning towards 
a more retail-led distribution model. This gives the 
platform greater control over sourcing quality, customer 
experience and execution standards. 
Technology-enabled onboarding and process visibility 
are supporting this transition, creating a more scalable 
framework for secured lending.
Growing a stronger lending ecosystem
PB Connect has built relationships across Public 
Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Housing Finance 
Companies and other financial institutions. The depth of 
these partnerships enables better policy visibility, faster 
query resolution and smoother movement of applications 
through the fulfilment journey.
A diversified partner network also allows PB Connect to 
adapt to changes in individual lenders' credit policies and 
lending appetite, helping maintain continuity of consumer 
access to secured credit.
We are scaling our secured lending proposition through stronger D2C play, combining digital sourcing, assisted 
fulfilment and a growing network of lending partners across Home Loans and LAP.

Policybazaar UAE
In 2018, PB Fintech’s decision to 
launch Policybazaar.ae in the UAE 
was motivated through our success in 
India. India had taught us a singular 
lesson: that when technology meets 
opacity, trust prevails. The UAE gave 
us an almost perfect mirror image 
of the opportunity we had seized at 
home, a large, rich, under-penetrated 
insurance market where products 
were sold, not selected, where the 
consumer’s voice was the weak link 
in the value chain, and where the 
move from analogue to digital was 
happening but far from finished.
Four pillars anchored the strategic 
case. First, the UAE’s expatriate 
composition, nearly 88% of its resident 
population, created a demographically 
familiar customer: mobile, digitally 
literate, financially aspirational, and 
perpetually underserved by traditional 
brokers who had never been required 
to truly compete for their attention. 
Second, Dubai’s ambition to become 
a global financial hub, codified in 
successive regulatory roadm

aps, 
signalled a governance environment 
that would reward compliant, 
technology-led intermediaries willing to 
build for the long term.
Third, PB Fintech had accumulated 
over a decade of experience, 
proprietary technology, and deep 
customer understanding from 
operating at scale in one of the world’s 
most complex insurance markets. 
Over the years, we had learned how 
to help people discover, understand 
and choose insurance in a way that 
felt relevant to their lives. That depth of 
capability could not be built overnight. 
It was a strength we were uniquely 
positioned to bring to the UAE. Fourth, 
and most strategically significant, 
the UAE was undergoing a quiet but 
consequential shift in how its residents 
related to the country itself. Dubai was 
no longer a temporary posting for the 
majority of its expatriate population. 
It had become home: a place where 
families were being raised, futures 
were being planned, and where 
financial protection was growing 
in direct proportion to the depth of 
those roots. Rising incomes, evolving 
lifestyles, and a generation of residents 
making long-term commitments to life 
in the UAE were creating a demand 
for insurance that went far beyond 
compliance. They were creating 
customers who actually wanted to be 
protected.
The Group’s thesis was not simply 
to replicate a comparison website 
in a new geography. PB Fintech 
had spent a decade building the 
technology, customer understanding, 
and operational depth to transform 
how people engage with financial 
products. The conviction was that 
these strengths could create a similar 
impact in the UAE, but only if they 
were thoughtfully adapted to the 
realities of the local market. This 
meant listening closely to customers, 
redesigning products and journeys 
around their needs, and building a 
team that understood the market 
from within. Policybazaar.ae was 
the proof of that conviction, and it 
remains the Group’s most important 
international demonstration

of what 
becomes possible when scale meets 
adaptability.

India's commercial insurance market is worth roughly 
₹1,20,000 Cr. It is large, it is growing and it is structurally 
underserved. The country has more than 63 million 
MSMEs contributing close to a third of GDP, and very 
few of them are properly insured. 
India’s commercial insurance market is large, but the 
experience remains fragmented. Many SMEs buy only 
what is mandatory, while larger companies often manage 
employee benefits, property, marine and liability through 
separate conversations. Product awareness is uneven, 
service remains manual and claims support varies by 
line.
We launched Policybazaar for Business in September 
2021, after more than a decade spent earning the trust 
of retail customers who had every reason to distrust 
the category. The gaps we found in B2B were ones we 
already knew how to close. Low product awareness. 
Fragmented claim

s servicing. Almost no digital 
infrastructure built for a corporate buyer.
The business serves large corporates through 
relationship-led portfolio management and SMEs through 
product-led online journeys supported by advisors. The 
model is deliberately hybrid because the purchase may 
be digital, but the risk often needs interpretation and the 
claim needs ownership.
In the four years operations, the business has grown 
the premium multifold. That makes us a serious broker 
by any measure, and still a very small share of a 
₹1,20,000 crore market. As digital adoption accelerates, 
technology-led brokers are steadily gaining share,

market share over time.

A group health policy is a promise made to people who 
did not choose it. An employee does not select the 
insurer, does not read the wording and in most cases 
does not know the sum insured until a relative is being 
admitted. Almost everything that matters about it is

settled in the forty-eight hours after a hospital asks for 
a pre-authorisation.
We do not treat claims as an after-sales function. Every 
client has a named claims contact rather than a helpdesk 
queue. Our own doctors sit inside the claims process 
rather than beside it, reviewing rejections and deductions 
before an employee sees them and arguing the medical 
case with the insurer where the file merits it.
A rejection that goes unchallenged is not a neutral 
outcome. It is a family paying a hospital bill that an 
insurer should have paid.
The rest of the work is unglamorous, and it is the whole 
job. Cashless approvals inside two hours. Turnaround 
monitored continuously rather than reported monthly. 
Weekly reviews with third-party administrators where 
files are escalated by name. A medico claims team that 
reads the discharge summary, not only the claim form.
Technology helps here in a narrower way than the word 
usually suggests. Most delay in an Indian health claim 
is caused not by slow decisions but by paperwork that 
was incomplete when it was submitted.

break-in inspection video covering the inspection location, lighting, 
odometer, windshield (cracks), chassis, a 360° damage view, engine

the insurer for issuance. The process required ~15 minutes per video and

detects an issue for the advisor to double-check. Results surface in the 
Advisor Panel with frame-level evidence and video seek timestamps.

instrument rather than a cost line.

An inclusive place to build a career
Diverse perspectives and an inclusive culture are treated as inputs to innovation, not as a compliance exercise. Progress is 
measured at every management level, and reported whether or not it flatters us.
Our approach
We are building a workplace where 
equal opportunity, mutual respect 
and a sense of belonging let every 
employee contribute. Our workforce 
grew to 28,330 in FY26, of whom 
approximately 24% are women. 
Women accounted for 25% of new 
hires during the year, strengthening 
the pipeline into the organisation.
Equitable progression
In FY26 the promotion rate for 
women (27%) was at par with men 
(26%) which is the clearest single 
indicator that progression is being 
managed on merit. Representation 
in leadership continued to improve: 
women hold 11% of senior 
management, 16% of middle

management and 15% of junior 
management roles. We recognise 
there is further to go, particularly 
in the senior tier, and are setting a 
quantified target with a timeline.
Pay equity
Equal pay for equal work is a 
governance matter, not a sentiment. 
We are establishing regular 
pay-equity review at each level, 
reporting the unadjusted gap, which 
reflects workforce composition, 
and the adjusted, like-for-like gap 
controlling for role, level, location 
and tenure. A like-for-like gap is 
remediated at the next cycle.
Inclusive employment
Our Equal Employment Opportunity 
Policy is aligned with the Rights of 
Persons with Disabilities Act, the 
Transgender Persons (Protection of 
Rights) Act and the HIV and AIDS 
Act. We employ 22 Persons with 
Disabilities, supported by inclusive 
recruitment and accessibility 
measures, with named liaison 
officers accountable.
Supporting new parents
We support new parents through 
enhanced maternity provisions, 
dedicated nursing rooms, a 
company-funded crèche across our 
India locations, and buddy-style 
return-to-work support for new 
mothers. The effect is visible in the 
return-to-work rate, which reached 
98% in FY26.
Targets To Set
We have not set quantified targets 
for gender representation, for 
women in senior management or 
for the employment of Persons 
with Disabilities. Our approach 
to date has been to build the 
underlying conditions first; 
namely equitable hiring, parity 
in progression, and a workplace 
that supports people through 
the stages of life at which 
representation is most often lost. 
That work is beginning to show: 
women accounted for 25% of new 
hires in FY26, the promotion rate 
for women (27%) was at par with 
men (26%), and the return-to-work 
rate after maternity leave reached 
98%. We recognise, however, 
that outcomes without targets 
are difficult to hold ourselves 
to, and that representation in 
senior management, at 11%, has 
further to travel. We will publish 
quantified diversit

y targets with 
defined timelines in the coming 
years, together with the baseline 
against which progress will be 
measured.

confidential access to our Employee

Career continuity

Rights, safety and the future of work
Human rights and workplace safety are material topics for PB Fintech. This page sets out the framework that governs them, 
the mechanisms through which concerns are raised, and what those mechanisms recorded in FY26.
Our commitment
Respect for human rights is 
embedded in our Code of Conduct 
and Human Rights related policies, 
which apply to all employees and 
are extended contractually to 
business partners and third-party 
service providers. They cover 
non-discrimination, freedom from 
harassment, freedom of association, 
prohibition of forced and child labour, 
safe working conditions, fair wages 
and privacy.
Due diligence
We operate a periodic human rights 
due diligence cycle: identify salient 
issues by function and geography, 
assess exposure across our own 
operations and our third-party 
workforce, act on findings through 
policy or process change, and track 
closure. Results are reported to the 
Board annually.
Salient issues identified
For a business of our shape, the 
salient risks concentrate in four 
places: workplace harassment 
in a young, largely field-based 
workforce; working hours and targets 
in sales roles; data privacy; and the 
working conditions of third-party and 
contracted staff.

Concerns can be raised through 
the reporting line, HR business 
partners, the POSH Committee, a

PB Fintech operates between millions of consumers and the 
institutions that provide insurance, credit and other financial 
products. We do not underwrite insurance or carry credit 
risk on our own balance sheet. Our ability to create value 
therefore depends on the quality of the relationships we 
build with customers, insurers, lenders, advisors, service 
partners, communities and institutions.
These relationships become valuable when they reduce 
information gaps, widen access, improve service outcomes 
and build confidence in financial products that are often 
complex and long term in nature. Over eighteen years, 
our role has expanded from helping customers compare 
products to supporting them across a broader financial 
lifecycle, from awareness and discovery to advisory, 
purchase, servicing, renewals and claims assistance.
Social and Relationship Capital is therefore not separate 
from our business model. It is one of the foundations on 
which the model operates.

beyond the transaction

CUSTOMERS
Financial products are promises about the future. Their value is often realised months or years after the original decision 
to buy. This makes trust particularly importan

t in insurance and credit, where customers must frequently make complex 
decisions with imperfect information.
Our customer relationship therefore begins with clarity. Policybazaar helps customers compare products, understand 
differences in benefits and conditions, and access advisory support across digital, telephonic, video and in-person 
channels. Paisabazaar extends the same principle to credit by helping consumers understand their credit profile before 
they borrow and by providing access to credit scores, credit-health insights and personalised recommendations.
Insurance earns trust most decisively at the time of claim. 
During FY26, Policybazaar supported 245,000+ health 
claims, with on-ground health claims assistance available 
in 250+ cities. Dedicated specialists guide customers 
through documentation, pre-authorisation, insurer and 
hospital coordination, discharge and post-claim support. 
Motor customers are supported through dedicated claim 
managers, while nominees under term policies receive 
specialised grief and claims assistance.
When The Promise Is Tested
Claims can sometimes be delayed or rejected because 
information is incomplete, documentation is insufficient 
or additional clarification is required. Claim Samadhaan 
creates a structured mechanism through which eligible 
cases can be reviewed again.
The process identifies rejected or pending cases, 
reconnects with customers, helps complete 
documentation and brings valid cases back to insurer 
partners for reconsideration.

The global economy remained resilient through 
CY2025 as inflation moderated, although trade 
and energy risks continued to shape the outlook. 
India’s real GDP grew 7.7% in FY2026, supported 
by broad-based domestic demand. Against this 
backdrop, insurance penetration remained 3.7% 
of GDP, indicating significant scope for deeper 
social security and formal credit.
Economic Overview
Economic Overview
Global Economy
The global economy growth stood at 3.5% in CY2025, 
unchanged from CY2024, while headline inflation 
moderated to 4.1%. Growth was supported by

resilient 
consumption, continued investment and the rapid 
reconfiguration of supply chains in response to higher 
trade barriers.
Advanced economies grew 1.9%, while emerging 
market and developing economies expanded 4.5% 
and contributed the larger share of global growth. This 
divergence continues to favour businesses exposed 
to large domestic markets in which consumption, 
urbanisation and infrastructure investment are still 
deepening.
The IMF projects global growth moderating to 3.0% in 
CY2026 before recovering to 3.4% in CY2027. Advanced 
economies are projected at 1.7% and 1.8%; emerging 
market and developing economies at 3.8% and 4.5%. 
The United States is expected to grow 2.2% and 2.1%, 
while the euro area is projected at 0.9% and 1.2% in 
CY26 and CY27. Expansion is expected to continue, but 
remain uneven across regions.
The principal risks remain geopolitical and policy-led. 
Disruption around the Strait of Hormuz could affect 
energy supply, freight costs and inflation, while tariff 
settings can change at short notice. Persistently higher 
energy prices would weaken household purchasing 
power and slow policy easing.
For PB Fintech, these effects are primarily indirect. 
Global rates influence treasury yields and risk appetite; 
energy costs affect domestic disposable incomes; and 
regional activity shapes the operating environment in 
the United Arab Emirates.

and wage pressure. With inflation above target in several 
major economies, monetary easing is expected to remain 
cautious and uneven, keeping global funding conditions 
relatively tight.
Indian Economy
India remained the fastest-growing major economy in 
FY2026, with real GDP expanding 7.7%, more than twice 
the global rate. Growth was broad-based and supported 
by domestic demand rather than a single export cycle.
Private final consumption expenditure accounted for 
61.5% of GDP, its highest share in more than a decade. 
A consumption-led economy progressively enlarges the 
market for protection, savings and credit as households 
acquire assets, assume longer-duration commitments 
and seek protection against mortality, morbidity and 
income shocks.
The sectoral composition reinforced the breadth of the 
expansion. Services gross value added grew 9.3%, 
led by financial, real estate and professional services, 
while manufacturing grew 10.7%. Favourable monsoons 
supported rural demand and widened the regional base 
for formal financial participation.
Low food inflation preserved purchasing power, while 
public investment, digital infrastructure and continued 
formalisation reduced the cost of identifying, underwriting 
and servicing customers. 
The banking system also entered this phase from 
strength. Its gross non-performing asset ratio fell to 
a multi-decade low of 1.8% in March 2026, improving 
lender confidence and capacity. Stronger asset quality 
supports the credit marketplace and, through healthier 
retail lending and asset formation, expands formal 
financial participation. Underwriting discipline remains 
essential.
India concluded negotiations on the India – European 
Union Free Trade Agreement and, in February 2026, 
announced a framework with the United States for an 
interim agreement. Both developments point to deeper 
market integration, more resilient supply chains and

a 
broader base for investment and employment.
The Outlook Ahead
Based on the Reserve Bank of India’s August 2026 
projection, real GDP is expected to grow 6.7% in 
FY2027. Although this represents moderation from the 
high FY2026 base, growth is expected to remain well 
above the global rate. Union Budget 2026 –27 continues 
to emphasise growth, capacity creation and inclusion.
Resilient household demand and moderating inflation 
should support protection, savings and credit. Energy 
prices, trade-policy changes and a slower global rate 
cycle remain the principal external risks to disposable 
incomes and financial conditions. The operating 
implication is to preserve underwriting and cost discipline 
while continuing to invest in access, advice and service.
Indian Life Insurance
India remained among the world’s ten largest 
life-insurance markets. Total life premium was 
approximately ₹9.97 lakh Cr, an increase of 12.5%. 
In FY2026, new business premium reached ₹4.60 
lakh crore, up 15.7%, while private insurers’ individual 
adjusted first-year premium increased 12% to ₹95,478 
Cr.
Life insurance represented 74.2% of total insurance 
premium in FY2025. Renewals accounted for 55.1% of 
life premium and new business for 44.9%, underscoring 
the importance of persistency, suitability and long-term 
service.
Indian General Insurance
General-insurance gross direct premium reached 
approximately ₹3.36 lakh crore in FY2026, an increase 
of 9.3% compared with 6.2% in FY2025. Health 
insurance, including personal accident, grew 15.4% 
and increased its share of sector premium to 40.8% 
from 38.6%.
The changing mix reflects greater awareness, 
medical-cost inflation and a protection gap that remains 
significant. Clear product comparison, appropriate 
coverage and dependable claims support will remain 
important to sustaining industry growth.
Key Regulatory Developments 
Parliament passed the Sabka Bima Sabki Raksha 
(Amendment of Insurance Laws) Act, 2025, amending 
the In

surance Act, 1938, the LIC Act, 1956 and the 
IRDA Act, 1999. The legislation raises the permitted 
foreign-investment limit in Indian insurers to 100%, 
simplifies registration and capital requirements, broadens 
operating flexibility and strengthens IRDAI’s supervisory 
and enforcement powers.
The changes are expected to improve access to 
capital, technology and specialist underwriting, thereby 
expanding market capacity. The benefits will depend on 
continued discipline in suitability, disclosure, grievance 
resolution and customer outcomes. 
The second material change was the GST exemption for 
individual life and health insurance premiums, effective 
22 September 2025. It applies to new business and 
renewals, lowering the cost of cover and supporting 
acquisition and persistency. For households managing 
several claims on income, a lower premium can be 
the difference between considering protection and 
postponing it. The measure also aligns with ‘Insurance 
for All by 2047’.
Insurance penetration remains 3.7% of GDP compared 
with a global average of 7.3%, while density is US$97. 
The gap is not only one of distribution. Households need 
products designed around irregular incomes, affordability 
constraints, pre-existing conditions and limited familiarity 
with insurance. The opportunity is to reach underserved 
customers with cover they can understand, afford and 
sustain.
Penetration should be interpreted with care because it 
is measured against GDP. In a fast-growing economy, 
the ratio can remain flat even while premiums and 
insured lives rise. The more important measure is 
whether protection is broadening across incomes and 
geographies, and whether customers remain covered 
through renewal and claims.

India’s low insurance intensity and uneven access to formal credit represent a significant long-term industry 
opportunity. Insurance penetration remained 3.7% in FY2025 and density was US$97, both well below global levels. 
The next phase of growth will depend on affordable, customer-centric products, trusted advice and service capable

INDUSTRY OVERVIEW
Protection and Credit Gaps Remain Significant
Protection and Credit Gaps Remain Significant
Insurance Market Size and Penetration
India’s insurance market is already large in absolute 
terms, but protection remains shallow relative to the 
size of its economy and population. In FY2025, insurers 
collected ₹11.93 lakh (LI + GI) Cr in premiums, paid 
₹8.36 lakh crore in claims. Based on the latest globally 
comparable data for 2024, India was the world’s 
10th-largest insurance market by premium volume. Yet it 
a

ccounted for only 1.8% of global premiums, highlighting 
the considerable headroom that remains.
Insurance penetration, which measures premiums 
as a share of GDP, provides another perspective on 
this opportunity. It increased from 3.3% in FY2015 to 
4.2% in FY2021 and FY2022, before moderating to 
3.7% in FY2024. Life insurance penetration stood at 
2.7%, compared with a global average of 3.0%, while 
non-life penetration was only 1.0%, against 4.3% 
globally. Nominal premiums have continued to grow, 
but not materially faster than the economy. Protection, 
therefore, is expanding in scale without deepening at 
the same pace.
The gap is even more visible on a per-capita basis. 
Insurance density in India was US$97 in FY2024, 
comprising US$72 for life insurance and US$25 
for non-life, compared with a global average of 
approximately US$943. The difference is particularly 
pronounced in non-life insurance, where demand for 
health, motor, property and commercial protection 
should rise as household incomes, asset ownership 
and formal economic activity expand.
Life insurance contributed approximately 74% of total 
premium in FY2025. Within non-life insurance, health 
was the largest business line at around 41% of gross 
domestic premium, reflecting greater awareness and 
rising healthcare costs.
The next phase of the industry’s development must 
therefore be measured not just by premium growth, 
but through growth in the number of households 
purchasing protection for the first time, the adequacy 
of cover, participation beyond major urban centres, 
policy renewals, service quality and claims outcomes. 
These measures will create a deeper and more durable 
financial resilience for the industry.
Mortality Protection Gap
Swiss Re estimates India’s mortality protection gap 
at 97%. This means only about 3% of the estimated 
protection need is insured; it is not a population-coverage 
statistic. The comparison remains wide even against 
China at 88% and the United Sta

tes at 82%.
Term insurance is designed for this gap, yet it is poorly 
understood and historically unattractive to a face-to-face 
seller. Low price, low awareness and a high need 
for explanation is precisely the combination in which 
transparent comparison and assisted digital advice can 
change category economics.

Affordability, Suitability and Advice
The insurance decision is shaped by affordability, 
familiarity, medical history, income stability and the ability 
to understand a future benefit today. These barriers are 
particularly relevant for first-time buyers, self-employed 
individuals, older customers and households without 
employer-sponsored cover.
Products therefore need to reflect actual payment 
patterns and coverage requirements. Monthly payment 
options, wider eligibility, appropriate waiting-period 
structures and relevant service support can influence 
whether a household enters and remains within the 
protection system.
Ad

vice is especially important in protection products. 
A lower premium may be accompanied by inadequate 
sum insured, while a broad feature list may obscure 
exclusions, co-payments or waiting periods. Customers 
need support in translating product terms into 
implications for the household balance sheet.
The value of advice continues after purchase. 
Renewal support helps maintain continuity, while 
claims assistance supports customers in navigating 
documentation, hospitals and insurers when the policy 
is tested. Trust is therefore built across the full policy 
lifecycle.
Retail Credit Penetration
Indicative international benchmarks place retail lending 
at 37% of GDP in India, compared with 61% in China, 
74% in the United States and 83% in the United 
Kingdom; the global average is 62%. Credit-card 
penetration is estimated at 5% in India, against 
approximately 35% globally. Although the estimates are 
dated, the direction of the gap remains clear.
The constraint is not only lender appetite. Thin or 
absent credit histories make risk harder to price, while 
customers may not know which products they are eligible 
for. Credit awareness, score improvement and eligibility 
matching therefore precede the loan itself.
A marketplace that begins with a free credit score can 
improve customer readiness, direct demand towards 
suitable lenders and help consumers build a record 
before the point of borrowing.
Industry Outlook
Economic growth creates households with more 
income and assets to protect, while a young population 
generates first-time financial decisions. Digital public 
infrastructure makes these households easier to 
identify, reach and serve. However, converting access 
into adequate protection and responsible formal credit 
remains incomplete.
Customers must discover a product, understand it, 
qualify for it and complete the process. Manufacturers 
must price risk, comply with regulation and service the 
contract. Both sides require support through repaym

ent, 
renewal, claims and grievance resolution.
Vertical platforms can connect these stages through 
common infrastructure for identity, payments and 
consented data while retaining category expertise. 
The opportunity therefore extends beyond online 
distribution: regulated partners, technology, advisors 
and service operations must work together to improve 
customer outcomes. Durable growth will depend on 
wider participation and trust.

Business Review
PB Fintech operates through two Core Online businesses: Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, and three New Initiatives: PB

service and claims.
The commercial logic is not diversification for its own sake. The businesses reach customers who prefer different routes to 
purchase for e.g. a digitally self-directed consumer, a household seeking in-person advice, an enterprise buying employee 
or commercial cover, or a UAE resident with cross-border needs. Sharing the underlying operating capabilities allows the 
Group to broaden access efficiently and use each interaction to improve future decisions.
During FY2026, growth was accompanied by discipline in business mix and execution. Protection formed a larger share of 
insurance; renewal and trail revenue expanded; and New Initiatives continued to scale while absorbing a greater proportion 
of their o

perating costs. Credit volumes were managed with greater restraint where portfolio quality required it.

BUSINESS REVIEW
Savings Insurance Business
During FY2026, the savings portfolio broadened 
the market-linked products like low-cost ULIPs, 
capital-guarantee solutions, child savings, retirement 
products and NRI investments through GIFT City. Savings 
premium recorded a four-year CAGR of 52%. The wider 
portfolio allowed advisors to begin with the customer’s 
goal, risk preference and time horizon.
Goal-based Planning
Goal-based propositions connect a policy to outcomes 
such as education or retirement. Under Waiver of Premium 
variants, if the insured customer dies, the insurer funds 
the remaining premiums and the planned maturity benefit 
continues, protecting the underlying financial objective.
Product and Advice Innovation
Waiver of Premium options help preserve continuity when 
future contributions are disrupted by an insured event, while 
capital-guarantee and traditional products provide greater 
certainty for customers seeking lower exposure to market 
volatility. Goal-based planning

compares the goal with 
available household resources before product selection.
Phygital Distribution
Customers may begin online and complete a needs 
assessment with an advisor in person. Output per Self-FOS 
advisor was twice that of an online-only advisor, indicating 
the continued relevance of assisted advice for larger, 
longer-duration commitments.
Portfolio Services
A digital portfolio view enables customers to track policies, 
switch allocations and review progress. 
Risk
Every life proposal is also assessed using 65 implicit and 
explicit  variables. Across term and savings, these controls 
averted ₹9,618 crore of potentially unviable sum-assured 
exposure during FY2026.
Motor and Others
Policybazaar’s private-car insurance business grew 
approximately three times faster than the underlying 
market. Two-wheeler insurance accelerated in the second 
half, with estimated market share of 11.8%. Motor remains 
an entry product for younger customers and supports a 
recurring renewal relationship.
Growth was supported by faster fulfilment and products 
linked to usage and driving behaviour. About 77% of motor 
policies are now issued within 3 hours.
Claims and Ownership Support
The Assured Delivery Programme, Q2FY25, launched in 
Q2FY25 uses curated garages, relationship managers and 
in-house quality checks. Till date, it has supported more 
than 30,000 customers across 185 cities and maintained 
satisfaction above 90%. 
PB Wheels launched in FY26 now extends engagement 
into ownership support by connecting customers with 
trusted workshops, servicing, inspections and value-added 
maintenance provide additional entry and renewal 
opportunities.
Product and Pricing Innovation
Pay-as-you-drive plans allow customers to select cover 
based on expected usage, while multi-year products reduce 
annual renewal requirements. Video-based inspection 
discounts, good-driver benefits and preferred-garage 
propositions use observable behaviour to improve pricing 
accuracy and

affordability.
Service Economics
Motor is a high-frequency category in which claims and 
renewal experience directly influence retention. Better 
inspection, garage coordination and post-sale visibility 
can reduce avoidable leakage for insurers while making 
the product easier for customers to use. The category also 
creates a regular point of re-engagement with younger 
households entering the broader insurance relationship.
Paisabazaar
Paisabazaar is the Group’s Online consumer-credit 
marketplace, providing access to credit scores, lending 
products and credit cards. By FY26, approximately 5.8 
Cr consumers had accessed a credit score through the 
platform. Cumulative transacting consumers reached 7.5 
million and completed transactions reached 11.3 million. 
During the year, the platform issued 3.5 lakh credit cards 
and sourced total credit disbursals (including secured 
credit) of ₹30,740 crore, an increase of 50% y-o-y. 
Core Online Credit
Core Online credit disbursals for FY26 were ₹9,474 crore, 
a decline of 20%, while revenue was ₹445 crore, down 
11%, reflecting tighter lender supply in unsecured credit. 
The business improved sequentially through the year; 
in Q4FY2026, Core Online disbursals increased 25% vs 
Q1FY26.
More than 70 lending partners are integrated with the 
platform. Quotes Engine combines Paisabazaar’s 
application and outcome history with lender scorecards to 
rank offers by approval probability and identify propositions 
better aligned with customer eligibility.
AI Paisa Picks applies a similar approach to more than 100 
credit-card propositions from 19 issuers and generates 
approximately 36,000 recommendations each day. Better 
matching can reduce unsuitable applications for consumers 
and processing leakage for lenders while preserving 
competition across the marketplace.
Paisabazaar’s proprietary risk layer declined approximately 
8% of customers that lender scorecards would otherwise 
have approved. The intervention reduced disbur

sal volume 
by approximately 10%; the declined cohort subsequently 
exhibited about three times the six-month delinquency of 
customers who passed the filter. Management accepted the 
near-term volume cost in support of a better-aligned book.
Credit Awareness and Progression
Credit information is often technical and difficult for 
consumers to interpret. Paisabazaar’s credit-progression 
strategy therefore begins with awareness. Free-for-life 
credit scores, monthly updates across all four credit 
bureaus, AI-generated video reports and Credit Health 
insights translate bureau data into plain language and 
identify actions customers can take to strengthen their 
credit profile. During FY2026, customers completed 
13.55 lakh credit-improvement transactions, while overall 
customer satisfaction increased to 91%.
For new-to-credit and emerging customers, understanding 
the score is only the first step. Paisa+, an FD-backed 
secured credit card launched with SBM Bank, provides a 
controlled entry point for establishing repayment history 
with limited risk exposure. Continuous monitoring and 
personalised insights then help customers improve their 
eligibility and, over time, graduate to mainstream credit. 
Together, these capabilities create an end-to-end pathway 
from understanding one’s credit position to improving it, 
building a formal credit record and accessing more suitable 
products.
Customer Engagement and Adjacent 
Products
Paisabazaar is extending the customer relationship beyond 
the initial loan disbursal. Deeper partner integrations enable 
returning customers to access repeat lending journeys with 
less friction, while bill payments, recharges and PB Wallet 
create more frequent reasons to engage with the platform. 
The relationship is also broadening beyond credit. Fixed 
deposits and bonds provide customers with options across 
liquidity, savings and investment needs. 
Over time, an integrated view of borrowing, liquidity 
and investments can support mo

re relevant lifecycle 
recommendations, positioning Paisabazaar as a continuing 
financial relationship rather than a platform used only at the 
point of borrowing.
PB Partners
PB Partners is PB Fintech’s advisor-enabled distribution 
platform, extending the Group’s insurance capabilities 
into markets where customers often prefer to complete 
a purchase through a trusted local advisor. The platform 
equips independent Point of Sales Person advisors 
with multi-insurer product access, digital onboarding 
and booking, needs-based recommendations, lifecycle 
servicing, training and relationship-manager support. The 
advisor contributes local reach and customer context; 
PB Partners provides the technology, product access 
and operating infrastructure required to serve customers 
consistently.
During FY2026, the network comprised approximately 
450,000 registered partners across nearly 19,000 pin codes, 
representing close to 99% of India’s pin-codes.
Around 80% of business was generated in Tier 2 and Tier 
3 markets. The platform worked with 45 insurer partners 
across motor, health and life insurance and maintained a 
diversified portfolio with a relatively high contribution from 
non-motor products.
Importantly, growth became more broad-based. Share of 
small partners in total premium is continuously increasing. 
A growing proportion of partners also began selling across 
more than one product category, indicating deeper platform 
adoption and the development of more durable advisory 
practices.
Policybazaar.ae
Policybazaar.ae premium grew 54% during FY2026 and 
was profitable for the full year. The annualised premium 
run-rate reached ₹1,980 Cr in Q4FY2026. The platform 
offers motor, health and life insurance from more than 35 
insurer partners; approximately half of premium now comes 
from non-motor categories.
Cross-border Product and Service Model
The proposition has been adapted to customers whose 
obligations span the UAE and India. Cross-border health, 
inco

me-protection and portability propositions address these 
requirements. In motor, claims assurance has become 
an integral part of the customer proposition. A network of 
partner garages, on-ground assistance and coordinated 
claims routing are improving the repair and settlement 
experience, supporting customer satisfaction, renewals and 
referrals.
PB for Business
PB for Business is the Group’s corporate and SME 
insurance New Initiative. It serves more than 50,000 clients 
through 13 operating centres and a presence across 130 
cities. Employee benefits is the principal entry product, 
creating recurring service requirements.
Product Portfolio
In addition to employee benefits, portfolio includes property, 
marine, engineering and liability cover. 
Service and Support: 
Smaller enterprises may require help identifying risks, 
comparing terms and coordinating documentation.
Relationship managers, in-house doctors and digital claims 
workflows provide continuing support. 
The employee-benefits ecosystem also provides enrolment, 
e-cards, claim filing, tracking and wellness through portals, 
an app and WhatsApp. Its support footprint extends across 
more than 130 cities and 14 languages, giving HR teams a 
service layer employees can use directly.

STRATEGY
Strategy
PB Fintech's strategy is to help customers make important financial decisions with greater confidence and remain 
supported after the transaction. Policybazaar and Paisabazaar are the Group's Core Online businesses. PB 
Partners, PB for Business and Policybazaar.ae extend these capabilities into advisor-led distribution, commercial 
insurance and the UAE. Their shared foundation includes technology, data, partner relationships, advice, service 
and claims support.
During FY26, the Group focused on protection-led growth, stronger recurring revenue and disciplined execution. 
Investment continued where customer parti

cipation and long-term value could increase.
1. 
 Protection-led and responsible growth
 
The Group's priority is to help families manage the 
financial consequences of illness, loss of income and 
the death of an earning member. In insurance, this 
means expanding access to health and term cover, 
improving affordability and encouraging adequate, 
continuing protection. Savings recommendations 
reflect a customer's goals, household resources 
and appetite for risk. In credit, growth is balanced 
with suitability, repayment capacity and a practical 
path towards formal borrowing. Progress is 
assessed through first-time participation, quality of 
cover, policy renewals, responsible repayment and 
customer experience. Policies that remain in force 
and loans that can be repaid are stronger measures 
of progress than transaction volume alone.
2. 
Trust through service and claims support
 
Trust is tested when a customer needs help, 
particularly during the time of claim. PB Fintech 
supports customers with documentation, 
pre-authorisation, hospital coordination, claim 
tracking, follow-up and grievance resolution. 
Multilingual and on-ground teams provide 
assistance, while technology helps identify missing 
information and service delays earlier. The Group's 
role is to help customers understand the claims 
process and receive timely support, while Insurers 
remain responsible for evaluating and settling 
claims. The aim is to remove uncertainty at difficult 
moments, so customers are not left to coordinate 
among the hospital, insurer and administrator 
alone. Claims experience also informs product 
communication, advisory and service improvements. 
Confidence in the claims journey influences whether 
families buy adequate cover, renew their policies 
and recommend insurance to others.
3. 
Collaborative innovation with partners
 
PB Fintech works with insurers, lenders and other 
regulated partners to develop products and journeys 
around needs that standard offeri

ngs do not always 
address. Customer feedback and operating data 
are combined with partner underwriting and product 
expertise to improve relevance, affordability and 
access. Recent innovations include unlimited 
sum insured plans, maternity benefits, more 
flexible payment options and solutions for women, 
homemakers, self-employed customers and NRIs. 
Collaboration also extends to documentation, 
product integrations and service workflows that 
reduce avoidable delays. The aim is to improve 
outcomes for customers while supporting stronger, 
more sustainable partner portfolios. This allows 
partners to expand access without weakening risk 
or service standards.
4. 
AI, Technology and Data driven approach
 
Technology, data and AI support customer matching, 
risk assessment, proposal completion, service, 
renewals and claims assistance. AI-generated 
explanations help make complex information usable; 
matching engines reduce irrelevant applications; 
risk models improve suitability; and workflow 
intelligence identifies incomplete proposals or 
potential service issues earlier. Automation improves 
routine execution, while advisors and service teams 
remain important where explanation or intervention 
is required. 
 
Opportunity
India's opportunity is not limited to moving existing financial transactions online. It lies in bringing more 
households and enterprises into formal protection and credit, improving the adequacy and suitability of the 
products they hold, and supporting them for longer. Rising incomes, formalisation and digital infrastructure have 
expanded access, but gaps remain in awareness, affordability, product understanding and continuing service.
For PB Fintech, this creates connected opportunities to expand participation, improve decisions and remain 
relevant through renewal, repayment, claims and changing financial needs. The opportunity follows a sequence: 
help a customer recognise a need, make a suitable product accessible, support completi

on and remain accountable 
after the transaction.
Expanding participation in protection
Large sections remain without adequate health or term 
cover, particularly first-time buyers, younger households, 
the self-employed, women, senior citizens and customers 
beyond major urban markets. Many households have the 
ability to pay but require propositions matched to irregular 
income, life stage, pre-existing conditions or unfamiliarity 
with insurance. Monthly payment options, broader health 
benefits and products designed around specific customer 
circumstances can make entry more practical. Progress 
also requires understandable terms, trusted advice and 
confidence in post-purchase support. Product co-creation, 
assisted journeys and service can therefore address 
barriers that distribution alone cannot solve.
Converting access into informed action
Access does not automatically produce a sound 
decision. Insurance remains complex to compare, while 
credit reports and eligibility criteria can be difficult to 
interpret. Personalised explanations, suitability-led 
recommendations, planning tools and assisted journeys 
can reduce the distance between information and action. 
Plain-language and video explanations can make credit 
information more usable, while track-and-manage 
journeys give customers a reason to return between 
borrowing events. In credit, this means helping 
customers understand their bureau information, improve 
readiness, establish repayment history and progress 
towards suitable mainstream products. Better matching 
also reduces unnecessary applications and processing 
leakage for partners.
Deepening existing customer relationships
A substantial part of the opportunity lies beyond the first 
transaction. Insurance renewals, credit progression, 
repeat lending, savings and investment products, and 
continuing service allow relationships to develop over 
time. Each year of persistency adds revenue without 
repeating the original acquisition effort, w

hile more 
frequent engagement provides better insight into 
changing protection, liquidity and borrowing needs. 
Claims assistance, renewal support and portfolio visibility 
can reinforce trust at the moments that determine 
whether a customer stays. Fixed deposits, bonds, 
payments and other adjacent products can extend the 
relationship where they solve a relevant need. The 
objective is lifecycle participation, not indiscriminate 
cross-selling.
Extending reach through complementary channels
Different customer segments require different modes of 
engagement. PB Partners combines digital infrastructure 
with the trust and continuing service of local advisors, 
particularly in Tier 2 and Tier 3 markets. PB for Business 
uses employee benefits as an entry point into wider 
corporate and SME risk requirements, supported by 
claims and service workflows. Policybazaar.ae adapts 
the Group’s proven model to the UAE, where customers 
share many of the same needs as those in India. Shared 
technology, integrations, risk intelligence and service 
infrastructure allow these businesses to broaden reach 
without recreating the entire operating platform for every 
channel or market. Their progress will be judged by 
contribution and customer outcomes, not reach alone.
Reinsurance Broking
Reinsurance broking can connect insurers and corporate 
clients with domestic and global capacity, support 
specialised risk placement and add fee income without 
placing underwriting risk on the Group's balance sheet. 
PB Fintech's insurance data and partner relationships can 
also support product design and placement insight. The 
opportunity will be developed with the same discipline 
applied to other New Initiatives.
Allied Opportunities
Regulated pathways and focused adjacencies
During FY26, the Group received an NBFC-Account 
Aggregator licence and approval for a Payment 
Aggregator licence, established a Policybazaar branch 
in GIFT City, and advanced Pensionbazaar, PB Wheels 
and PB P

ay. These activities remain early-stage. Their 
relevance lies in extending journeys the Group already 
serves through consent-based financial insight, lower 
payment friction, retirement solutions and mobility 
services. Progress will be assessed against customer 
relevance, regulatory fit, capital intensity and sustainable 
economics.
Trust, governance and people
Trust underpins every part of our strategy. 
For customers, it requires transparent information, suitability-led advice, dependable service and support when a claim 
or grievance arises.  For partners, it requires fairness, transparency and a shared commitment to the long-term health 
of the ecosystem. For regulators, it requires responsible conduct, appropriate controls and timely compliance.
Our people translate these commitments into everyday decisions. We seek to attract, develop and retain professionals 
who combine category expertise with a strong sense of customer responsibility. An intrapreneurial culture encourages 
autonomy and innovation, accompanied by clear accountability for outcomes. Sharing effective practices across 
businesses enables the Group to learn faster while preserving the specialist capabilities required in each market.

Risk Management, Governance 
and Sustainability
As PB Fintech has grown from a pioneering digital web 
aggregator into a diversified fintech ecosystem, our 
risk framework has changed with it. What began as a 
functional necessity has become a strategic imperative.
At the heart of this evolution is our commitment to 
managing risk not as a constraint but as a cor

e lever 
of innovation, resilience and trust. As India's financial 
landscape expands in complexity and scale, so does 
the need for robust, forward-looking oversight that is 
adaptive by design and unified in purpose.
Risk Governance Across a Multi-Entity, 
Multi-Licence Business
Our risk framework is built as a Group Risk Architecture, 
anchored on the following pillars.
1. Three Lines of Defence Model
Line 1: Business ownership of risk, with controls 
embedded in day-to-day operations
Line 2: An independent Risk and Compliance function 
reporting to the Group CRO
Line 3: Internal Audit, reporting directly to the Audit 
Committee
2. Entity-Specific Risk Management
Each licensed entity operates under its own governance 
framework, aligned to the expectations of its regulator. 
IRDAI governs insurance broking in India, IFSCA 
governs insurance intermediation at the IFSC, CBUAE 
governs our UAE operations, and RBI governs account 
aggregation, payments and digital lending. All of them 
sit within a single group-wide risk taxonomy, which lets 
us manage interdependencies and concentration risk in 
one view.
3. Integrated Risk Themes
• 
Technology and Cyber Risk: cloud-native controls, 
penetration testing and incident response readiness
• 
Regulatory Risk: continuous alignment with evolving 
regulation, including DPDP, data privacy, digital 
lending and SRO norms
• 
Consumer Risk: suitability of advice and timely 
grievance redressal, supported by AI-assisted 
monitoring
• 
Reputational and ESG Risk: societal trust, 
responsible use of data and the impact metrics we 
report
• 
Financial and Credit Risk: capped guarantee 
exposures and lending activity, governed within a 
defined risk appetite
• 
Localisation of compliance protocols, so that KYC, 
AML and data sovereignty requirements meet the 
standards of each host regulator
• 
A centralised risk policy engine and governance 
dashboard, giving executive management and the 
Board a consistent view
• 
Stress-testing fo

r new verticals such as PB Health, 
with particular focus on provider integration and 
patient data security
• 
Partnership risk models for embedded finance and 
APIs, including capped arrangements with our lending 
partners
Looking Ahead: Risk as a Catalyst
Our purpose-driven risk strategy is enabling us to:
• 
launch responsibly and scale with trust 
• 
create digital journeys that are frictionless and 
compliant
• 
deliver embedded risk intelligence to customers and 
partners
• 
anticipate risks rather than only respond to them, 
particularly in GenAI, financial inclusion and digital 
infrastructure
PB Fintech Risk Framework: Evolution 
and Structure
As we move from digital aggregation to digital 
infrastructure, our risk framework is no longer only a 
gatekeeper. It has become a strategic compass. It keeps 
us resilient in uncertainty, compliant in complexity and, 
above all, trusted by the customers and ecosystems we 
serve.
We continue to evolve by design and expand with 
purpose, and risk excellence remains central to our 
growth journey. As the Group becomes more layered 
across licences, geographies and partnerships, the 
framework is built to scale with it, through a common 
taxonomy, common escalation paths and a single view 
of exposure at the Board.
Culture and Accountability
A framework works only where behaviour supports it. 
Risk ownership sits with business leaders rather than 
with the control functions that monitor them. Escalation 
is treated as expected rather than exceptional, and 
speaking up is protected. Training on conduct, data 
handling and regulatory obligations is refreshed each 
year and tracked to completion across the Group.

Dear Member(s),
Your Directors takes pleasure in presenting the Eighteenth (18th) 
Annual Report covering the highlights of the finances, business 
and operations of the PB Fintech Limited (“the Company”). Also 
included herein are the Audited Financial Statements (standalone 
& consolidated) prepared in compliance with Ind AS Accounting 
Standards and the Auditor’s Report thereon for the financial year 
ended March 31, 2026.
Company overview and State of 
Company affairs
With its flagship brands, Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, PB 
Fintech has revolutionized India’s online landscape for insurance 
and credit products. Both the platforms are India’s leading online 
marketplaces in their respective domains. The brands help 
Indian middle-class households secure social security. Beyond 
the market leadership, they serve as catalysts for advancing 
financial inclusion across India by fostering greater financial 
literacy and awareness. This commitment forms a cornerstone 
of PB Fintech’s social mission, contributing significantly to the 
broader goals of social welfare and economic development. By 
bridging gaps in access to financial products and services, PB 
Fintech fosters greater economic participation and resilience 
among diverse segments of the population. We have also 
ventured into reinsurance brokerage, payment aggregation & 
account aggregation businesses. The company’s initiatives, PB 
Partners, PB for Business and Policybazaar.ae are also continuing 
to strengthen their position and economics. Collectively, these 
expansions

into adjacent areas complement our core offerings by 
enriching the value we deliver, driving innovation, and enhancing 
customer satisfaction.
Policybazaar is a dedicated insurance marketplace committed to 
empowering the Indian middle-class families protect themselves 
against the financial impact of the life’s uncertainties – 3Ds (Death, 
Disease & Damage). Registered as a Composite Broker with 
IRDAI, we are a one-stop solution for all insurance needs. We 
provide comprehensive insurance solutions to customers and 
assist our customers in product discovery, seamless purchase 
experiences, policy management support and claims assistance 
and risk management solutions. The Company also supports 
insurers across the reinsurance placement lifecycle, including risk 
assessment, program structuring, market placement, negotiation 
and renewal planning. We have also commenced business 
operations in our Insurance Intermediary office in Gift city post 
receipt of approval from IFSCA on 15th April 2025.
Paisabazaar is a leading digital marketplace for financial products, 
offering consumers seamless access to compare and avail 
credit, investment, savings, and payment solutions through its 
website and mobile app. Leveraging its AI-powered technology 
platform and partnerships with banks, NBFCs and other financial 
institutions, the Company provides personalised recommendations 
and end-to-end digital fulfilment. Since 2017, Paisabazaar has 
partnered with all four credit bureaus to drive credit awareness 
by providing free credit scores and credit improvement services, 
benefiting over 58 million consumers across 850+ cities and towns 
by FY 2025–26. FY26 marked an important milestone in this 
journey with the launch of Bonds and Fixed Deposits, expanding 
the platform beyond credit to enable consumers to borrow, save, 
and invest within a trusted ecosystem. The Company follows the 
RBI’s Digital Lending Guidelines, maintains a robust grievance 
redressal mechanism, is I

SO/IEC 27001:2022 certified.
PB Partners is an enablement platform for over 450K independent 
insurance sellers. It is based on a B2A2C (Business to Agent 
to Consumer) approach. PB Partners thrives on the strength of 
our collaborations. Our dedicated partners are the driving force 
behind our mission to revolutionize India’s insurance industry. By 
leveraging advanced technology, our partners play a crucial role 
in reaching underserved and remote areas, bringing essential 
coverage to those who need it most. Together, we work to open 
new markets, connect with diverse demographics, and provide 
personalized solutions. Our commitment to innovation and 
excellence helps streamline processes, reduce paperwork, and 
enhance claims settlement.
PB for Business is a comprehensive platform for corporates & 
SMEs for their insurance needs. The platform helps businesses 
mitigate risks, safeguard employee well-being, and drive long-term 
resilience through smarter insurance solutions. We offer products 
that include both employee benefits as well as non-employee 
benefits, and we have covered over 50k large corporates & SMEs. 
Our platform delivers real-time quote visibility, seamless insurer 
comparison, and enhanced sales efficiency through streamlined 
digital journeys. Serving startups, SMEs, and large corporates, the 
platform provides customized advice and integrated solutions from 
a single source.
Policybazaar.ae has emerged as the leading digital distributor in 
the UAE, solidifying our market leadership. We have developed 
innovative solutions that directly address the unique needs of Non-
Resident Indians (NRIs) and cross-border residents. Partnerships 
with leading regional insurers & lenders have strengthened 
our credibility and broadened our portfolio, making us a trusted 
marketplace for customers seeking value and choice. We work 
with over 35 insurance partners and 10+ lenders to provide 
unbiased advisory and unique products to our consumers.

the Secretarial Auditors have not reported any instance 
of fraud in relation to the Company by its officers or

subsidiaries, Paisabazaar Marketing and Consulting

made thereunder, the auditors reported the matter to 
the Central Government and the Audit Committee of 
Paisabazaar.

terminated the services of the alleged employee and 
recovered INR 97 lakhs subsequent to the year end.

corrective actions. The incident has no material impact 
on the Company beyond the amount determined.

Dear Stakeholders,
At PB Fintech, our journey has been driven by a singular purpose to make financial products simple, accessible and transparent for 
every Indian. Over the years, we have witnessed the rapid evolution of the digital financial services ecosystem, creating unprecedented 
opportunities to expand financial inclusion while strengthening customer trust. As we continue to scale our business, we remain 
committed to creating sustainable value by embedding responsible business practices into every aspect of our operations.
We believe that sustainable growth is built on the foundation of trust. Trust earned through transparent customer engagement, ethical 
conduct, sound governance, technological innovation and a relentless focus on delivering value. These principles have shaped our 
organisation since inception and continue to guide every strategic decision we make.
As a technology-led enterprise, innovation remains our greatest strength. We conti

nuously invest in digital capabilities to simplify complex 
financial decisions, improve customer experiences and enable greater access to insurance, credit and other financial solutions. However, 
innovation can only be meaningful when supported by robust governance. Accordingly, we continue to strengthen our enterprise risk 
management framework, reinforce cybersecurity measures, protect customer data and ensure compliance with evolving regulatory 
expectations.
Our people remain central to our success. We are committed to fostering an inclusive, diverse and performance-driven workplace where 
every individual is empowered to contribute, learn and grow. By nurturing a culture built on integrity, collaboration and continuous learning, 
we seek to develop future-ready talent capable of driving long-term innovation.
While our business model has a relatively lower direct environmental footprint compared to traditional industries, we recognise that 
environmental responsibility extends beyond operational boundaries. We continue to pursue opportunities to optimise resource efficiency, 
encourage responsible consumption and integrate environmental considerations into our day-to-day operations. We believe that every 
responsible decision contributes to building a more sustainable future.
Equally important is our responsibility towards society. By improving access to financial protection and enabling informed financial 
choices, we aim to contribute meaningfully to India’s broader agenda of financial inclusion. We believe that technology, when deployed 
responsibly, has the power to bridge gaps, create opportunities and improve financial resilience for millions of individuals and families.
As we look ahead, we will continue to innovate with purpose, operate with integrity and place our customers and stakeholders at the 
centre of every decision. Together, we remain committed to building a resilient organisation that not only delivers sustainable business 
performance but a

lso creates lasting positive impact for society.
On behalf of the Board and the leadership team, I extend my sincere gratitude to our customers, employees, business partners, 
shareholders and regulators for their continued trust and support. We look forward to shaping the next phase of PB Fintech’s journey with 
responsibility, resilience and purpose.

PRINCIPLE 1 - Businesses should conduct and govern themselves with integrity, and 
in a manner that is Ethical, Transparent and Accountable
PB Fintech is committed to conducting its business with the highest standards of ethics, integrity, transparency, and 
accountability. As a technology-driven financial services platform, the Company recognizes that customer trust is 
the cornerstone of its business and therefore places strong emphasis on responsible corporate governance, ethical 
conduct, regulatory compliance, and robust risk management.
The Company’s governance framework is designed to promote responsible decision-making, safeguard stakeholder 
interests, and ensure compliance with applicable laws, regulations, and industry standards. The Board of Directors, 
supported by its various Committees, provides strategic oversight on governance, risk management, compliance, 
and sustainability-related matters, reinforcing accountability across all levels of the organization.
PB Fintech has established a comprehensive framework of policies, codes, and internal controls that guide ethical 
business conduct across its operations. These include the Code of Conduct, Code for Prevention of Insider Trading, 
Anti-Bribery and Anti-Corruption Policy, Whistle Blower Policy, Related Party Transactions Policy, Risk Management 
Policy, Information Security Policy, Data Privacy Policy, and other governance policies. Employees, directors, and 
business associates are expected to uphold these principles while performing their respective responsibilities.
Recognizing the importance of trust in digital financial services, the Compa

ny continues to strengthen its information 
security and cybersecurity framework through robust technological safeguards, access controls, security monitoring, 
and periodic assessments. These measures help protect customer information, maintain the confidentiality of 
sensitive data, and enhance operational resilience.
PB Fintech remains committed to maintaining the highest standards of governance through continuous policy 
reviews, regular compliance monitoring, internal audits, and oversight by the Board and its Committees. By 
embedding ethical business practices into its strategy, operations, and stakeholder interactions, the Company aims 
to create sustainable long-term value while reinforcing trust among customers, employees, investors, regulators, 
and business partners

PRINCIPLE 2 - Businesses should provide goods and services in a manner that is 
sustainable and safe
PB Fintech is committed to delivering technology-enabled financial products and services that are accessible, 
transparent, secure, and responsible. Through its digital platforms, including Policybazaar and Paisabazaar, 
the Company enables customers to make informed financial decisions by providing access to a wide range of 
insurance, credit, and other financial products from multiple partners. The Company’s customer-centric approach 
focuses on simplifying financial choices, promoting transparency, and enhancing financial inclusion through 
technology-driven solutions.
As a digital-first organization, PB Fintech recognizes that the quality, safety, and reliability of its services are 
fundamental to maintaining customer trust. The Company continually invests in technology, product innovation, 
cybersecurity, and data privacy to provide secure digital experiences while safeguarding customer information. 
Robust quality assurance processes, platform monitoring, and continuous system enhancements support service 
reliability and operational resilience.
The Company collaborates with insurers, lending institutions, and other business

partners to facilitate responsible 
product offerings while encouraging fair business practices across its ecosystem. PB Fintech also leverages data 
analytics and digital capabilities to improve customer experience, enhance product discovery, and support informed 
decision-making through transparent product information and comparison tools.
Being an asset-light, technology-enabled business, the Company’s direct environmental footprint is relatively 
limited. Nevertheless, PB Fintech remains committed to improving operational efficiency through responsible 
resource management, digitization of processes, paperless transactions, and adoption of environmentally conscious 
workplace practices, thereby minimizing its environmental impact.
The Company also recognizes the importance of responsible innovation in the evolving digital financial services 
landscape. By embedding governance, information security, privacy, and customer-centric design into its products 
and services, PB Fintech seeks to create sustainable long-term value for customers, business partners, investors, 
employees, and society.

PRINCIPLE 3 - Businesses should respect and promote the well-being of all 
employees, including those in their value chains
PB Fintech recognizes that its employees are fundamental to its long-term success and ability to deliver innovative, 
technology-enabled financial solutions. The Company is committed to fostering a workplace that promotes 
respect, inclusion, diversity, employee well-being, and continuous learning, while providing equal opportunities for 
professional growth and development.
The Company strives to create a work environment founded on integrity, mutual respect, and meritocracy, where 
employees are empowered to contribute their ideas, develop their capabilities, and achieve their full potential. Its 
human resource practices are designed to attract, develop, and retain talent through fair employment practices, 
performance-driven career progression, and continuous capability building.
Employee well-being remains a key priority. PB Fintech promotes a safe, healthy, and supportive work environment 
through comp

rehensive health and safety measures, wellness initiatives, and employee assistance programmes. 
The Company also encourages open communication and employee engagement through structured feedback 
mechanisms, regular interactions with leadership, and grievance redressal channels that enable employees to raise 
concerns without fear of retaliation.
The Company is committed to fostering an inclusive workplace that values diversity across gender, age, 
background, experience, and perspectives. Equal opportunity principles are embedded across the employee 
lifecycle, including recruitment, learning and development, performance management, and career advancement. PB 
Fintech maintains a zero-tolerance approach towards discrimination, harassment, and any form of unfair treatment, 
supported by appropriate policies and governance mechanisms.
Recognizing the dynamic nature of the financial technology sector, PB Fintech continues to invest in learning and 
development initiatives aimed at enhancing technical capabilities, leadership competencies, regulatory awareness, 
cybersecurity, and professional skills. These initiatives support employees in adapting to evolving business 
requirements while strengthening organizational resilience and innovation.
Beyond its direct workforce, the Company seeks to promote responsible employment practices across its value 
chain by encouraging vendors, service providers, and business partners to comply with applicable labour laws, 
uphold ethical employment practices, and maintain safe and respectful working conditions.
Through its people-first approach, PB Fintech remains committed to building an engaged, inclusive, and high-
performing workforce while creating long-term value for employees, customers, shareholders, and society.

PB Fintech is committed to fostering a fair, transparent, and respectful workplace where 
employees can raise concerns without fear of retaliation. To support this commitment, the 
Company has established a comprehensive Employee Grievance Redressal Policy, which 
provides a structured framework for employees to report workplace grievances and appeal 
decisions, while ensuring confidentiality, impartiality, and adherence to the principles of 
natural justice.
Governance Framework
Grievance Redressal Committees (GRCs) have been constituted in accordance with 
the Company’s Employee Grievance Redressal Policy to review and address employee 
grievances in a fair, timely, and transparent manner.
Grievance Reporting Channels
Employees may submit grievances or appeal decisions through multiple accessible 
channels, including:
• 
Official Company email; 
• 
PB Support, the Company’s digital employee helpdesk available on the intranet, which 
enables employees to register and track grievances through an online ticketing system. 
Fair and Confidential Resolution Process
The Company ensures that all grievances are handled with the highest standards of 
confidentiality, safeguarding the privacy of all individuals involved. Every complaint is 
reviewed objectively and impartially, with due regard to the principles of natural justice and 
procedural fairness.
As part of the inquiry process:
• 
The respondent is

formally notified of the allegations through a written communication 
outlining the details of the complaint. 
• 
Both the complainant and the respondent are provided a fair opportunity to present 
their respective views, submit supporting evidence, and, where appropriate, identify 
witnesses to support their case. 
• 
The Grievance Redressal Committee endeavours to complete investigations within a 
reasonable timeframe while ensuring a thorough and impartial review. 
Outcome and Corrective Action
Upon completion of the inquiry, the Committee submits its findings and recommendations 
to the designated authority, including the Human Resources Head or the appropriate 
Committee Head, for consideration and necessary action. Appropriate corrective or 
disciplinary measures are determined based on the findings of the inquiry and the severity 
of the matter.
Depending on the nature of the violation, disciplinary actions may include verbal 
counselling, written warnings, reprimands, or termination of employment or contractual 
engagement, where warranted.
Documentation and Record Management
The Company maintains comprehensive documentation of grievance proceedings and 
inquiry outcomes in a secure and confidential manner. Relevant records, including 
investigation reports and disciplinary actions, are retained in accordance with the 
Company’s record management practices and applicable legal requirements.

To ensure efficient and timely resolution of complaints, the company has established a structured internal 
escalation process. This process ensures that all grievances are addressed within a defined turnaround time 
(TAT). If complaints exceed this TAT, they are escalated to higher authorities for further attention. Policybazaar 
has a clear system and procedure in place for receiving, registering, and resolving grievances, with the 
following minimum timeframes for response:
• 
First-time response: The company aims to send a written response to the complainant within 2 hours of 
receiving the grievance.
• 
Details in the response: The initial response includes the name of the officer responsible for handling the 
grievance, along with details of the issue raised and the follow-up TAT for resolving the complaint.
• 
Resolution within TAT: If the complaint is resolved within the stipulated time, the resolution an

d 
acknowledgment are communicated to the customer.
• 
Interim updates: If the complaint is not resolved within the specified days, the company is required to 
share an interim update with the customer, explaining the delay and providing a new expected resolution 
time.
• 
Non-response from customer: If the customer does not respond to calls and emails three times, the 
complaint is closed, and an interim closure email is sent. The complaint can be reopened if the customer 
responds later.
